Machine-readable comparison: `docs/data/primary-eos-refits.json` (this record's identifier).

This record uses the self-consistent Sokolova et al. (2013) pressure-scale fit: Table 1 supplies reference volume/composition inputs and Table 4 supplies the final Holzapfel and thermal coefficients. The fit jointly considers shock-wave, ultrasonic, X-ray diffraction, dilatometric, and thermochemical measurements; it is not derived from one experimental dataset. Sokolova et al. (2016) republishes the parameters and supplies the executable Excel/VBA implementation, reference-temperature convention, and corrected equations, rather than a new fit dataset. The publications do not provide individual parameter errors, parameter covariance, or a complete machine-readable list of fit points and weights. A source-constrained reconstruction nevertheless combines 392 room-temperature comparison observations for all eleven markers in one shared Equation (20) objective against the pointwise mean of the precursor Table 2 Holzapfel and Table 3 Vinet isotherms, with Table 4 retained as a post-calibration closure test. This tests the coupled cross-calibration and is not an independent refit of the eleven EOS coefficient sets. The \*\_sokolova\_2013 identifier names the scientific fit year; the 2016 workbook remains explicit in source\_lineage as the implementation and correction source.

Parameter covariance is not supplied.

No numerical 298 K fit dataset, weights, coefficient covariance, or confidence level for the Table I coefficient errors is published in the inspected article and supplement. The upper/lower isotherm rows describe separate envelope fits, not coefficient errors or independent 298 K observations. A refit of the published 298 K EOS is not possible with the current information. Fratanduono explicitly describes the Gruneisen prescription for reducing measured stress to the principal isentrope, but does not explicitly specify the Debye isentrope-to-298 K calculation used in our diagnostic. Applying Kraus (2016) Eq. (16), its Debye caloric model, and theta0=343.5 K is our inference, not a confirmed reproduction of the 2020 reduction. The 53 candidate points also use an unconfirmed graphical Hugoniot input and omit 46 higher-compression rows. Their 1.562 GPa RMS agreement with the published curve does not establish recovery of the original data, coefficient parity, or a superior EOS.

- **Note:** Equation, central 298 K coefficients, printed errors, density reference and phase checked directly against the final primary article and official supplemental PDF.
- **Audit date:** 2026-09-08
- **Verified fields:** equation; parameters; units; reference\_state; phase; published\_uncertainties; validity
- **Primary source check:**
    - **Access URL:** https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.124.015701
    - **DOI:** 10.1103/PhysRevLett.124.015701
    - **Locations:** Table I, page 015701-3, central 298 K isotherm row and caption; Supplemental Section S4, Eq. (2), page S2; Supplemental Section S5 and Table S1
    - **Finding:** The exponent is eta\*y+beta\*y^2+psi\*y^3 with y=1-(rho0/rho)^(1/3); rho0=8.939 g/cm3. Table I prints separate central and upper/lower-envelope fits.
    - **Source artifacts:**
        - **Url:** https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.124.015701
        - **Sha256:** 18db9d32504e10007a7927c04c5610a5dbf25a4088577d14c0bab0033804a412
        - **Url:** https://journals.aps.org/prl/supplemental/10.1103/PhysRevLett.124.015701
        - **Sha256:** cdf0985112a5584a7a97c187ea2683d1fc6740761db8851ae9cb5b489a9ff98c
- **Primary data check:**
    - **Status:** parameterization\_only
    - **Audit date:** 2026-09-08
    - **Dataset identifiers:** None declared
    - **Source locations:** Table I; Supplemental S4-S5 and Table S1
    - **Finding:** Table S1 contains reduced-isentrope observations, not 298 K isothermal rows. No numerical 298 K fit dataset, weights, coefficient covariance, or confidence level for the Table I coefficient errors is published in the inspected article and supplement. The upper/lower isotherm rows describe separate envelope fits, not coefficient errors or independent 298 K observations. A refit of the published 298 K EOS is not possible with the current information. Fratanduono explicitly describes the Gruneisen prescription for reducing measured stress to the principal isentrope, but does not explicitly specify the Debye isentrope-to-298 K calculation used in our diagnostic. Applying Kraus (2016) Eq. (16), its Debye caloric model, and theta0=343.5 K is our inference, not a confirmed reproduction of the 2020 reduction. The 53 candidate points also use an unconfirmed graphical Hugoniot input and omit 46 higher-compression rows. Their 1.562 GPa RMS agreement with the published curve does not establish recovery of the original data, coefficient parity, or a superior EOS.
    - **Reconstruction attempt:**
        - **Status:** partial\_thermal\_reconstruction\_without\_parameter\_parity
        - **Resource:** docs/data/fratanduono-2020-cu-thermal-reduction.json
        - **Script:** scripts/reproduce\_fratanduono\_2020\_cu.py
        - **Note:** Kraus (2016) Eqs. (11), (12), and (16) supply a Debye reduction route. Seven compressed source rows use the explicitly adopted low-compression gamma law; 46 more have a candidate reduction using the digitized Figure S2 Hugoniot. The last 46 compressed rows lack graphical Hugoniot coverage. Neither diagnostic fit recovers the published coefficients; these qualified pressures are not registered as original 298 K fit data.

<details markdown="1">
<summary>Parameter provenance</summary>

- **Origin of the parameterization:** Fratanduono (2020), Table I and Supplemental S4: isotherm reduced from measured ramp compression. Stress and thermal reductions are part of the experimental inference, not an independent ab-initio EOS fit.
- **V0:** Table I caption and S4: rho0=8.939 g/cm3; V0=4\*63.546/(rho0\*0.602214076) angstrom^3/conventional cell. Molar mass is a conversion convention, not a fitted source parameter.
- **K0:** Table I, central 298 K isotherm: 133.6 +/- 0.8 GPa
- **Eta:** Table I, central 298 K isotherm: 6.29 +/- 0.8
- **Beta:** Table I, central 298 K isotherm: 2.06 +/- 0.4
- **Psi:** Table I, central 298 K isotherm: 1.65 +/- 0.6

</details>

### copper\_dewaele\_2004\_table1\_compression

- **Description:** All 42 Table I copper atomic-volume observations, with both printed ruby-pressure reductions.
- **Kind:** pressure\_volume
- **Reference:**
    - **Authors:** Dewaele; Loubeyre; Mezouar
    - **Year:** 2004
    - **Source:** Phys. Rev. B
    - **Volume:** 70
    - **Locator:** 094112
    - **DOI:** 10.1103/PhysRevB.70.094112
- **Source location:** Table I, journal page 094112-4
- **Associated EOS records:** copper\_dewaele\_2004\_mao\_ruby\_vinet; copper\_dewaele\_2004\_vinet\_1; copper\_dewaele\_2019\_mao\_vinet; copper\_dewaele\_2019\_dor\_vinet
- **Notes:** Table I groups Cu/W/Al in the first two runs and Au/Pt/Ta in the last three runs. Blank metal cells are omitted rather than imputed. P\_R is the classical Mao et al. (1986) reduction (A=1904 GPa, B=7.665); P'\_R is the Dewaele et al. revision (A=1904 GPa, B=9.5). The paper states a common 0.01 angstrom^3/atom volume uncertainty and a pressure uncertainty increasing from 0.05 GPa at 1 GPa to 2 GPa at 150 GPa, but prints neither row-wise pressure errors nor raw R1 wavelengths.

[Observation resource](https://github.com/CPrescher/peritheos/blob/main/peritheos/data/datasets/copper-dewaele-2004-table1-compression.csv)
